lessons: Keep the reviewed design: DispatchPause with discard_hold supersession, latest-wins, stale-lifecycle refusal, the decision-before-mutation probe, the drain fresh/retry release test, and the CLI Drain-kwargs dormancy probe. Start from the prior branch; the last retry had to restore it by hand.

Criterion 1 test is circular: it writes its own `if await pause.allow_offer(): accounting.append`. Add optional `pause: DispatchPause | None = None` to the daemon admission path (DispatchAdmission or the compose_daemon_dispatch `dispatch` closure) and consult it before snapshot() and create_task.

admit() is sync and returns a task, so await allow_offer() in the async dispatch closure (or an async admission wrapper) before calling admit. Test the real path: while paused, no snapshot is taken and no task is created; an already-admitted task still completes.

Keep the daemon pause default None so production stays dormant. Extend the dormancy test to assert that the composed daemon dispatch carries no pause, giving pause-resume-activation a concrete assertion to flip.

Drain: after _wait_for_offer returns, re-check `self._clock() - started >= ceiling` before _draw_retry and before dispatch, and on expiry take the existing timer_fired/_halted path. Add a test: a pause that outlasts the ceiling admits nothing after release.

Remove the zero-delay `_yield_control` default. When pause is given, require wait_for_control (raise if missing) or default to a real-interval sleep through the injected clock seam. No hot loop that re-folds the journal.
Stay inside the fence. Do not edit test_daemon_tasks.py or test_control.py. Run both Verification commands.
